## Syntax and conventions

- **High:** `𗝘` terminates a clause/sentence. A chat message can contain several such clauses.
- **High:** The common clause skeleton is `C 𘎙 P 𗇋 X 𗢘 Y 𗝘`, with optional material and occasionally only one argument. `P` is a predicate/property expression; X and Y are its arguments. This is a structural interpretation, not a recovered English word order.
- **High:** `𗇋` separates the predicate/header from argument material; `𗢘` separates argument fields. Exact grammatical labels (subject/object versus topic/value) are **medium** confidence.
- **Medium:** `𘎙` marks an assertion/declaration; `𘀿` marks a request/question. Requests can use `𗬀` to identify an addressee.
- **Medium:** `𗧟`, `𘍰`, `𗎧`, `𗖉` select clause classes. Working glosses respectively are observation/entity, relation/property, action/control, and quantity/value. # 1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED

This is a partial reconstruction, not a claim to have recovered the complete dictionary. Confidence labels apply to the decoding, not to whether an agent's statement was true. Untranslated glyphs below are retained as identifiers for unknown words or objects.

## Syntax and conventions

- **High:** `𗝘` terminates a clause/sentence. A chat message can contain several such clauses.
- **High:** The common clause skeleton is `C 𘎙 P 𗇋 X 𗢘 Y 𗝘`, with optional material and occasionally only one argument. `P` is a predicate/property expression; X and Y are its arguments. This is a structural interpretation, not a recovered English word order.
- **High:** `𗇋` separates the predicate/header from argument material; `𗢘` separates argument fields. Exact grammatical labels (subject/object versus topic/value) are **medium** confidence.
- **Medium:** `𘎙` marks an assertion/declaration; `𘀿` marks a request/question.
- **Medium:** `𗬀` introduces an addressee/destination/target field, often followed by a literal agent ID in requests. Its exact range of uses is unknown. It is distinct from attribution marker `𗉁`.
- **Medium:** `𗧟`, `𘍰`, `𗎧`, `𗖉` select clause classes. Working glosses respectively are observation/entity, relation/property, action/control, and quantity/value. Their exact names and meanings are unknown. They may instead be lexical namespaces, so the same following glyph need not have the same meaning in every class.
- **Medium:** `𗉁` introduces an attribution/owner/source field. Literal `agent_n` strings are allowed and denote the corresponding agents. In #28 the attributed item is itself another glyph, not a literal agent ID.
- **Medium:** `𘒍 ... 𗳯` brackets embedded/quoted clauses. Embedding can nest (#14, #41).
- **Low:** `𗝒` introduces an additional qualification or embedded assertion.
- **Medium:** `𗘓` introduces an additional qualifier/status. Its following tokens `𗭎` and `𘔃` contrast in otherwise similar relation clauses; **low-confidence** candidate senses are yes/possible versus no/impossible.
- **Low:** `𘁅` is an index/location/time qualifier, perhaps “at/in.” Its followers `𘒾`, `𗶁`, `𗋄` might identify successive stages (0, 1, 2), but that numeric mapping is not established.
- **Low:** `𘖨` links clauses or conditions, possibly “after/with.”
- **Low:** `𗠫` may mark negation/correction. In #53 it is inserted before `𘎙` in a clause otherwise repeating #28; “not” is a candidate, not a recovered word.
- **Low:** `𗃐` may be a prospective/intention modality (#70), possibly announcing an intended action. Its exact meaning is unknown.
- **Medium confidence as a structural distinction; low confidence semantically:** `𘆋` is an alternate modality/header marker in action-class clauses (#66/#69), replacing the usual `𘎙`; its force is unknown.
- **High:** `⊘` represents a discarded out-of-alphabet message; its intended content cannot be reconstructed.

## Recurrent vocabulary: cautious working glosses

- **Medium:** `𗶢` expresses a classification/type/description relation. It often has X followed by `𗙥`; source attribution is optional. Exact sense unknown; existence/presence/status remains an alternative to literal “type.”
- **Medium:** In the `𗖉` class, `𗕥` gives a value/measurement of its argument. Values recur in a small vocabulary, but exact numbers are unknown.
- **Medium-low:** In the `𗎧` class, `𗃁` denotes an action on an object, tentatively activate/use. Movement is an alternative interpretation.
- **Low:** In the action class, `𗹾` describes an effect/dependency. It repeatedly relates an object to an embedded `𗃁` action.
- **Low:** In the relation class, `𗐢(agent,target)` concerns access/visibility/availability/reachability. No particular one of these senses is established.
- **Low:** In the relation class, `𗋄(description,identifier)` may give a name/equivalence (#34). This does not establish the meaning of `𗋄` in other positions.
- **Low:** `𗕛` before a value may be a negative sign; `𗢻` may be an arithmetic/comparison connector.
- **Low:** `𗬏 𗲕 X` and `𗬏 𗋄 X` are related parameterized quantities, possibly old/new or stage-indexed values. Neither component has an established English sense.

## Syntax and conventions

- **High:** `𗝘` terminates a clause/sentence. A chat message can contain several such clauses.
- **High:** The common clause skeleton is `C 𘎙 P 𗇋 X 𗢘 Y 𗝘`, with optional material and occasionally only one argument. `P` is a predicate/property expression; X and Y are its arguments. This is a structural interpretation, not a recovered English word order.
- **High:** `𗇋` separates the predicate/header from argument material; `𗢘` separates argument fields. Exact grammatical labels (subject/object versus topic/value) are **medium** confidence.
- **Medium:** `𘎙` marks an assertion/declaration; `𘀿` marks a request/question.
- **Medium:** `𗬀` introduces an addressee/destination/target field, often followed by a literal agent ID in requests. Its exact range of uses is unknown. It is distinct from attribution marker `𗉁`.
- **Medium:** `𗧟`, `𘍰`, `𗎧`, `𗖉` select clause classes. Working glosses respectively are observation/entity, relation/property, action/control, and quantity/value. Their exact names and meanings are unknown. They may instead be lexical namespaces, so the same following glyph need not have the same meaning in every class.
- **Medium:** `𗉁` introduces an attribution/owner/source field. Literal `agent_n` strings are allowed and denote the corresponding agents. In #28 the attributed item is itself another glyph, not a literal agent ID.
- **Medium:** `𘒍 ... 𗳯` brackets embedded/quoted clauses. Embedding can nest (#14, #41).
- **Low:** `𗝒` introduces an additional qualification or embedded assertion.
- **Medium:** `𗘓` introduces an additional qualifier/status. Its following tokens `𗭎` and `𘔃` contrast in otherwise similar relation clauses; **low-confidence** candidate senses are yes/possible versus no/impossible.
- **Low:** `𘁅` is an index/location/time qualifier, perhaps “at/in.” Its followers `𘒾`, `𗶁`, `𗋄` might identify successive stages (0, 1, 2), but that numeric mapping is not established.
- **Low:** `𘖨` links clauses or conditions, possibly “after/with.”
- **Low:** `𗠫` may mark negation/correction. In #53 it is inserted before `𘎙` in a clause otherwise repeating #28; “not” is a candidate, not a recovered word.
- **Low:** `𗃐` may be a prospective/intention modality (#70), possibly announcing an intended action. Its exact meaning is unknown.
- **Medium confidence as a structural distinction; low confidence semantically:** `𘆋` is an alternate modality/header marker in action-class clauses (#66/#69), replacing the usual `𘎙`; its force is unknown.
- **High:** `⊘` represents a discarded out-of-alphabet message; its intended content cannot be reconstructed.

Seven invalid attempts were accumulated, all before stage 2. The public messages do not give the task statement or establish whether stage 3 is terminal success.

# 4. EVIDENCE

1. **Clause boundaries and slots:** Repeated constructions in #7/#8, #18/#20/#23, and #62/#63 put `𘎙`, `𗇋`, `𗢘`, `𗝘` in stable positions while arguments vary. This is strong structural evidence, independent of the task's identity.
2. **Declaration/request contrast:** `𘀿` often occurs with explicit agent targets and repeated prompts (#41, #44, #49, #50). `𘎙` occurs in repeated descriptions and reported values. This supports, but does not prove, an assertion versus request/question distinction. Repeated `𗬀 agent_n` in requests supports an addressee/destination marker, distinct from `𗉁` attribution.
3. **Attribution:** `𗉁 agent_n` follows otherwise similar type-like clauses (#4, #7, #8, #14, #16, #18, #20, #22, #23, #25, #62, #63). This supports a source/owner field rather than an ordinary predicate argument. The non-agent use in #28 prevents confidently narrowing it to “speaker.”
4. **Embedding:** #26, #34, #38, #56 and #57 contain an internal action-shaped clause between `𘒍` and `𗳯`; #14/#41 appear to nest them. This supports bracket-like quotation/subordination.
5. **Value-like expressions:** `𗖉 𘎙 𗕥 𗇋 X 𗢘 Y` has a small recurring output vocabulary. Agent_3's same X=𘝲 receives changing Y at #25/#33/#48/#51/#54/#60. This supports a value/state measurement, not a fixed unique name.
6. **Do not assume global object identity:** #8 and #7 give different values for 𗔛; #62 and #63 give different outputs for the apparently same compound involving 𗪥. Possible explanations include private scope, omitted agent indexing, class/color references, different semantics of the quantity expressions, or errors by the agents. None is settled.
7. **Action/access sequence:** Requests directed to agent_3 about 𗂶 are followed by that agent's ACT(𗂶); later ACT(𗝭) and access-like relation to 𗮿 precede the next transition. This motivates activation/access glosses, but physical movement remains possible.
8. **Qualifier contrast:** #38 and #50 refer to agent_7 and the same described object, but end with `𗘓𗭎` versus `𗘓𘔃`. A changing yes/no or availability status is plausible. Different spatial/role qualifications are also possible.
9. **Possible stage indices:** `𘁅𘒾` appears early, `𘁅𗶁` in #25, and `𘁅𗋄` repeatedly in the last stage. More specifically, the same unresolved referent `𗀮` appears with `𘁅𘒾` in #4 and with `𘁅𗋄` in #59/#66. This cross-version recurrence strengthens a temporal/indexed interpretation beyond mere stage correlation. It remains insufficient to map the tokens to 0/1/2, particularly because those glyphs occur elsewhere.
10. **Minimal contrast and modalities:** #53 repeats #28's action clause `𗥬(𗝭,𘚂)` with only `𗠫` inserted before `𘎙`. This makes negation/correction plausible, though not established. `𘆋` in #66/#69 and `𗃐` in #70 occupy modality-like positions; only the latter's final-action context suggests prospective/intention, and that gloss is weak.
11. **Numerical restraint:** The changing state and signed-looking expressions allow many numerical assignments. We have not recovered a consistent digit table. A guessed numeric solution would not establish decoding.
12. **What would change these conclusions:** A reliable English sense for one repeated visual/property compound could distinguish spatial navigation from control-panel activation. Independent evidence of numeral values could test the arithmetic and stage-index hypotheses. Evidence that the four clause prefixes select unrelated dictionaries would favor namespaces over semantic classes. A task/interface description might help ground referents, but should not be mistaken for evidence of the messages' exact intended meaning.

# 1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED

This is a partial reconstruction, not a claim to have recovered the complete dictionary. Confidence labels apply to the decoding, not to whether an agent's statement was true. Untranslated glyphs below are retained as identifiers for unknown words or objects.

## Syntax and conventions

- **High:** `𗝘` terminates a clause/sentence. A chat message can contain several such clauses.

- **High:** The common clause skeleton is `C 𘎙 P 𗇋 X 𗢘 Y 𗝘`, with optional material and occasionally only one argument. `P` is a predicate/property expression; X and Y are its arguments. This is a structural interpretation, not a recovered English word order.
- **High:** `𗇋` separates the predicate/header from argument material; `𗢘` separates argument fields. Exact grammatical labels (subject/object versus topic/value) are **medium** confidence.
- **Medium:** `𘎙` marks an assertion/declaration; `𘀿` marks a request/question.
- **Medium:** `𗬀` introduces an addressee/destination/target field, often followed by a literal agent ID in requests. Its exact range of uses is unknown. It is distinct from attribution marker `𗉁`.
- **Medium:** `𗧟`, `𘍰`, `𗎧`, `𗖉` select clause classes. Working glosses respectively are observation/entity, relation/property, action/control, and quantity/value. Their exact names and meanings are unknown. They may instead be lexical namespaces, so the same following glyph need not have the same meaning in every class.
- **Medium:** `𗉁` introduces an attribution/owner/source field. Literal `agent_n` strings are allowed and denote the corresponding agents. In #28 the attributed item is itself another glyph, not a literal agent ID.
- **Medium:** `𘒍 ... 𗳯` brackets embedded/quoted material, including clauses and possibly bare phrases/tokens. Embedding can nest (#14, #41).
- **Low:** `𗝒` introduces an additional qualification or embedded assertion.
- **Medium:** `𗘓` introduces an additional qualifier/status. Its following tokens `𗭎` and `𘔃` contrast in otherwise similar relation clauses; **low-confidence** candidate senses are yes/possible versus no/impossible.
- **Low:** `𘁅` is an index/location/time qualifier, perhaps “at/in.” Its followers `𘒾`, `𗶁`, `𗋄` might identify successive stages (0, 1, 2), but that numeric mapping is not established.
- **Low:** `𘖨` links clauses or conditions, possibly “after/with.”
- **Low:** `𗠫` may mark negation/correction. In #53 it is inserted before `𘎙` in a clause otherwise repeating #28; “not” is a candidate, not a recovered word.
- **Low:** `𗃐` may be a prospective/intention modality (#70), possibly announcing an intended action. Its exact meaning is unknown.
- **Medium confidence as a structural distinction; low confidence semantically:** `𘆋` is an alternate modality/header marker in action-class clauses (#66/#69), replacing the usual `𘎙`; its force is unknown.
- **High:** `⊘` represents a discarded out-of-alphabet message; its intended content cannot be reconstructed.

Evidence that the four clause prefixes select unrelated dictionaries would favor namespaces over semantic classes. A task/interface description might help ground referents, but should not be mistaken for evidence of the messages' exact intended meaning.
